days.day: Saint Martin of Tours, Bishop on Wednesday of week 32 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Saint Martin of Tours
days.week: Wednesday of week 32 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And it came to pass, as he was going to Jerusalem, he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
And as he entered into a certain town, there met him ten men that were lepers, who stood afar off;
And lifted up their voice, saying: Jesus, master, have mercy on us.
Whom when he saw, he said: Go, shew yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass, as they went, they were made clean.
And one of them, when he saw that he was made clean, went back, with a loud voice glorifying God.
And he fell on his face before his feet, giving thanks: and this was a Samaritan.
And Jesus answering, said, Were not ten made clean? and where are the nine?
There is no one found to return and give glory to God, but this stranger.
And he said to him: Arise, go thy way; for thy faith hath made thee whole.

saint.name: Saint Martin of Tours
saint.about: A Roman soldier who, on a freezing night at a city gate, cut his military cloak in half with his sword and gave half to a beggar. That night he dreamed of Jesus wearing the half cloak. He left the army, became a monk and then the bishop of Tours, and spent his life with the poor.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Were not ten made clean? and where are the nine?

days.title: SAY THANK YOU
days.t: Ten got healed. One came back to say thank you. Be the one.
days.where: Luke's Gospel has a soft spot for outsiders. On the road to Jerusalem, ten men with leprosy, a skin disease that forced you to live apart from everyone, beg Jesus for mercy. The one who comes back to thank him is a Samaritan, the outsider of the group.
days.means: Everybody wants the blessing. Hardly anybody comes back to say thanks. Gratitude is part of being healed, not an extra, and the outsider is the one who gets it right. Jesus notices who comes back.
days.today: Text the person who helped you this year and actually thank them.
days.say: Jesus, You've done more for me than I've noticed. Thank You. Make me the one who comes back. Amen.

days.day: Saint Josaphat, Bishop, Martyr on Thursday of week 32 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Saint Josaphat
days.week: Thursday of week 32 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And being asked by the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come? he answered them, and said: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:
Neither shall they say: Behold here, or behold there. For lo, the kingdom of God is within you.
And he said to his disciples: The days will come, when you shall desire to see one day of the Son of man; and you shall not see it.
And they will say to you: See here, and see there. Go ye not after, nor follow them:
For as the lightening that lighteneth from under heaven, shineth unto the parts that are under heaven, so shall the Son of man be in his day.
But first he must suffer many things, and be rejected by this generation.

saint.name: Saint Josaphat
saint.about: A bishop in what's now Ukraine and Belarus who spent his life working to bring Eastern Christians back into unity with Rome. It cost him: a mob killed him for it in 1623. He was the first saint of the Eastern Churches to be canonized by Rome.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: For lo, the kingdom of God is within you.

days.title: IT'S ALREADY IN YOU
days.t: Stop waiting for a sign from the sky. God's kingdom is already here, starting in you.
days.where: The Pharisees, religious leaders who kept the law strictly, ask Jesus when God's kingdom is finally coming. They expect a big public show. Jesus tells them it doesn't work like that.
days.means: God's kingdom isn't a date on a calendar or a place you have to chase. It starts inside you and shows up in how you treat the people right next to you. Don't run after every voice saying it's over there.
days.today: Skip chasing the next big thing for one day. Do the good thing right in front of you.
days.say: Jesus, You're already here. Grow Your kingdom in me, starting with how I treat people today. Amen.

days.day: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini on Friday of week 32 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini
days.week: Friday of week 32 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And as it came to pass in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.
They did eat and drink, they married wives, and were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark: and the flood came and destroyed them all.
Likewise as it came to pass, in the days of Lot: they did eat and drink, they bought and sold, they planted and built.
And in the day that Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man shall be revealed.
In that hour, he that shall be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away: and he that shall be in the field, in like manner, let him not return back.
Remember Lot’s wife.
Whosoever shall seek to save his life, shall lose it: and whosoever shall lose it, shall preserve it.
I say to you: in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
Two women shall be grinding together: the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left: two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be keft.
They answering, say to him: Where, Lord?
Who said to them: Wheresoever the body shall be, thither will the eagles also be gathered together.

saint.name: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini
saint.about: An Italian nun who came to New York in 1889 to help Italian immigrants nobody else was looking after. She built schools, orphanages and hospitals across the Americas, became a U.S. citizen, and was the first American citizen to be named a saint. She's the patron saint of immigrants.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Whosoever shall seek to save his life, shall lose it: and whosoever shall lose it, shall preserve it.

days.title: DON'T LOOK BACK
days.t: Don't freeze up looking back at what you're leaving. Hold your life loose and you get to keep it.
days.where: Jesus talks about the end of time and points back to Noah's flood and to Lot leaving the city of Sodom, when people were busy living like nothing would ever change. Lot's wife looked back at what she was leaving and froze.
days.means: Life can change in one night, so don't spend it gripping what you already have. The tighter you hold your life for yourself, the more you lose it. Spend it on God and other people, and you keep it.
days.today: Let go of one thing you keep looking back at.
days.say: Jesus, I'm holding on too tight. Help me let go and follow You forward. Amen.

days.day: Saturday of week 32 in Ordinary Time or Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
days.name: Saturday of week 32 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Saturday of week 32 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And he spoke also a parable to them, that we ought always to pray, and not to faint,
Saying: There was a judge in a certain city, who feared not God, nor regarded man.
And there was a certain widow in that city, and she came to him, saying: Avenge me of my adversary.
And he would not for a long time. But afterwards he said within himself: Although I fear not God, nor regard man,
Yet because this widow is troublesome to me, I will avenge her, lest continually coming she weary me.
And the Lord said: Hear what the unjust judge saith.
And will not God revenge his elect who cry to him day and night: and will he have patience in their regard?
I say to you, that he will quickly revenge them. But yet the Son of man, when he cometh, shall he find, think you, faith on earth?

saint.name: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saint.about: On Saturdays with no other feast, the Church can honor Mary. The old tradition is that on the first Holy Saturday, when everyone else had lost hope, Mary kept believing.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: We ought always to pray, and not to faint.

days.title: KEEP ASKING
days.t: Keep praying. Don't give up on it, even when nothing seems to move.
days.where: Jesus tells a story about a widow who keeps showing up at a crooked judge's door until he finally gives her justice. In those days a widow had almost no power. All she had was not giving up.
days.means: If even a bad judge gives in to someone who won't quit, God, who actually loves you, is listening. Prayer isn't one shot. Keep showing up. Jesus ends by asking if he'll find that kind of faith when he comes back.
days.today: Pick one thing you stopped praying about and bring it back today.
days.say: God, I'm still asking. Don't let me give up on You, and thank You for never giving up on me. Amen.

days.name: 33rd Sunday in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: For even as a man going into a far country, called his servants, and delivered to them his goods;
And to one he gave five talents, and to another two, and to another one, to every one according to his proper ability: and immediately he took his journey.
And he that had received the five talents, went his way, and traded with the same, and gained other five.
And in like manner he that had received the two, gained other two.
But he that had received the one, going his way digged into the earth, and hid his lord’s money.
But after a long time the lord of those servants came, and reckoned with them.
And he that had received the five talents coming, brought other five talents, saying: Lord, thou didst deliver to me five talents, behold I have gained other five over and above.
His lord said to him: Well done, good and faithful servant, because thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will place thee over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
And he also that had received the two talents came and said: Lord, thou deliveredst two talents to me: behold I have gained other two.
His lord said to him: Well done, good and faithful servant: because thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will place thee over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
But he that had received the one talent, came and said: Lord, I know that thou art a hard man; thou reapest where thou hast not sown, and gatherest where thou hast not strewed.
And being afraid I went and hid thy talent in the earth: behold here thou hast that which is thine.
And his lord answering, said to him: Wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sow not, and gather where I have not strewed:
Thou oughtest therefore to have committed my money to the bankers, and at my coming I should have received my own with usury.
Take ye away therefore the talent from him, and give it to him that hath ten talents.
For to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound: but from him that hath not, that also which he seemeth to have shall be taken away.
And the unprofitable servant cast ye out into the exterior darkness. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Well done, good and faithful servant... enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

days.title: USE WHAT YOU GOT
days.t: Whatever God put in your hands, use it. Don't bury it because you're scared.
days.where: Matthew's Gospel, a few days before Jesus dies. He tells a story about a man who leaves his servants his money while he travels. A talent was a huge amount, about twenty years of wages, and it's where our word talent comes from.
days.means: God gave everybody something, not the same amount and not the same thing. The only one who gets in trouble is the one who buried his out of fear. Use what you've got, even if it feels small.
days.today: Make the thing you've been sitting on. Post it, play it, send it.
days.say: God, thank You for what You put in my hands. Help me use it instead of hiding it. Amen.

days.day: Monday of week 33 in Ordinary Time or Saint Margaret of Scotland or Saint Gertrude, Virgin
days.name: Monday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Monday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: Now it came to pass, when he drew nigh to Jericho, that a certain blind man sat by the way side, begging.
And when he heard the multitude passing by, he asked what this meant.
And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
And he cried out, saying: Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me.
And they that went before, rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried out much more: Son of David, have mercy on me.
And Jesus standing, commanded him to be brought unto him. And when he was come near, he asked him,
Saying: What wilt thou that I do to thee? But he said: Lord, that I may see.
And Jesus said to him: Receive thy sight: thy faith hath made thee whole.
And immediately he saw, and followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

saint.name: Saint Margaret of Scotland
saint.about: A queen of Scotland who fed the poor at her own table, built churches and raised eight children. She was known for getting up at night to pray and for giving away whatever she could. Today is also the day for Saint Gertrude, a German nun and mystic.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: What wilt thou that I do to thee? But he said: Lord, that I may see.

days.title: LORD, LET ME SEE
days.t: Jesus asks what you want. Be honest. Ask to really see.
days.where: Near the end of Luke, Jesus passes through Jericho on his way to Jerusalem. A blind man begging by the road hears the crowd, figures out who it is, and starts yelling for him. People tell him to be quiet. He gets louder.
days.means: The crowd tried to shut him up and he wouldn't stop. Jesus stops for him and asks a real question: what do you want? Don't be shy with God. Ask for what you actually need, even just to see your own life clearly.
days.today: Answer Jesus's question honestly: what do you want Him to do for you?
days.say: Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me. Lord, let me see. Amen.

days.day: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, Religious on Tuesday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
days.week: Tuesday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And entering in, he walked through Jericho.
And behold, there was a man named Zacheus, who was the chief of the publicans, and he was rich.
And he sought to see Jesus who he was, and he could not for the crowd, because he was low of stature.
And running before, he climbed up into a sycamore tree, that he might see him; for he was to pass that way.
And when Jesus was come to the place, looking up, he saw him, and said to him: Zacheus, make haste and come down; for this day I must abide in thy house.
And he made haste and came down; and received him with joy.
And when all saw it, they murmured, saying, that he was gone to be a guest with a man that was a sinner.
But Zacheus standing, said to the Lord: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have wronged any man of any thing, I restore him fourfold.
Jesus said to him: This day is salvation come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

saint.name: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
saint.about: A princess who married young, loved her husband, and spent her money feeding the hungry and building a hospital. After he died she gave up royal life to care for the sick and the poor, and she died at 24. The story goes that she was caught carrying bread to the poor in her cloak, and when she opened it, it was full of roses.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: This day is salvation come to this house.

days.title: HE'S COMING OVER
days.t: Jesus picked the guy everybody hated and invited himself over. Nobody's too far gone for a visit.
days.where: In Jericho, Zacchaeus is a rich tax collector, which back then meant working for the Romans and skimming off your own people. He's short, so he climbs a sycamore tree just to see Jesus over the crowd.
days.means: Jesus doesn't wait for Zacchaeus to clean up first. He calls him by name and comes to his house, and that's what changes him: he gives half of what he owns to the poor and pays back four times what he cheated. Being seen by God changes you.
days.today: Make something right with somebody you owe, money or an apology.
days.say: Jesus, come to my house today, mess and all. Change what needs changing. Amen.

days.day: Wednesday of week 33 in Ordinary Time or Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul, Apostles or Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne
days.name: Wednesday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Wednesday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: FIRST READING
verses: And in the sight of the throne was, as it were, a sea of glass like to crystal; and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four living creatures, full of eyes before and behind.

And the first living creature was like a lion: and the second living creature like a calf: and the third living creature, having the face, as it were, of a man: and the fourth living creature was like an eagle flying.

And the four living creatures had each of them six wings; and round about and within they are full of eyes. And they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.
And when those living creatures gave glory, and honour, and benediction to him that sitteth on the throne, who liveth for ever and ever;
The four and twenty ancients fell down before him that sitteth on the throne, and adored him that liveth for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying:
Thou art worthy, O Lord our God, to receive glory, and honour, and power: because thou hast created all things; and for thy will they were, and have been created.

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: As they were hearing these things, he added and spoke a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately be manifested.
He said therefore: A certain nobleman went into a far country, to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
And calling his ten servants, he gave them ten pounds, and said to them: Trade till I come.
But his citizens hated him: and they sent an embassage after him, saying: We will not have this man to reign over us.

And it came to pass, that he returned, having received the kingdom: and he commanded his servants to be called, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.
And the first came, saying: Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.
And he said to him: Well done, thou good servant, because thou hast been faithful in a little, thou shalt have power over ten cities.
And the second came, saying: Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.
And he said to him: Be thou also over five cities.
And another came, saying: Lord, behold here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin;
For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up what thou didst not lay down, and thou reapest that which thou didst not sow.
He saith to him: Out of thy own mouth I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up what I laid not down, and reaping that which I did not sow:
And why then didst thou not give my money into the bank, that at my coming, I might have exacted it with usury?
And he said to them that stood by: Take the pound away from him, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.
And they said to him: Lord, he hath ten pounds.
But I say to you, that to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound: and from him that hath not, even that which he hath, shall be taken from him.
But as for those my enemies, who would not have me reign over them, bring them hither, and kill them before me.
And having said these things, he went before, going up to Jerusalem.

saint.name: Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul
saint.about: Rome's two great churches stand over the tombs of the apostles Peter and Paul. Honoring the buildings is really honoring the faith those two died for. In the U.S. it's also the day for Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne, a French nun who came to the American frontier in her fifties to teach. The Potawatomi called her the woman who prays always.

key.label: FIRST READING
key.v: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.

days.title: HOLY, HOLY, HOLY
days.t: The words you sing at every Mass are being sung in heaven right now, nonstop.
days.where: Revelation, also called the Apocalypse, is the vision of heaven given to John, written for Christians who were being persecuted. Here he sees God's throne with living creatures around it who never stop singing. The Church sings their song at every Mass, right before the Eucharist.
days.means: When you sing the Holy, Holy at Mass, you're joining a song that's already going in heaven. Worship isn't something we made up. It's us catching up to what heaven is already doing.
days.today: Next time you're at Mass, sing the Holy, Holy like you mean it. Or say it slow once today.
days.say: God, You're holy and I'm not, and You still want me close. Today I'll praise You the way heaven does. Amen.

days.day: Thursday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Thursday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Thursday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And when he drew near, seeing the city, he wept over it, saying:
If thou also hadst known, and that in this thy day, the things that are to thy peace; but now they are hidden from thy eyes.
For the days shall come upon thee, and thy enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and straiten thee on every side,
And beat thee flat to the ground, and thy children who are in thee: and they shall not leave in thee a stone upon a stone: because thou hast not known the time of thy visitation.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: If thou also hadst known, and that in this thy day, the things that are to thy peace; but now they are hidden from thy eyes.

days.title: HE CRIED OVER THE CITY
days.t: Jesus looks at the city he loves and cries. Peace was right in front of it and it missed it.
days.where: Jesus is coming down the Mount of Olives toward Jerusalem, a few days before he dies. The crowd is celebrating, and he stops and weeps, because he can see the city is going to turn him away. About forty years later the Romans did tear Jerusalem down.
days.means: God doesn't watch us blow it with his arms crossed. He cries over it. The visit is today, not someday, and the things that bring peace are usually sitting right there if we stop long enough to see them.
days.today: Name one thing that actually brings you peace, and make time for it today instead of later.
days.say: Jesus, don't let me miss you when you show up. Open my eyes to what brings me peace today. Amen.

days.day: Friday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Friday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Friday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And entering into the temple, he began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought.
Saying to them: It is written: My house is the house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.
And he was teaching daily in the temple. And the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people sought to destroy him:
And they found not what to do to him: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: My house is the house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.

days.title: HE FLIPPED THE TABLES
days.t: Jesus walks into the Temple and throws the sellers out. God's house is for prayer, not a hustle.
days.where: This is right after Jesus rides into Jerusalem, days before he dies. The Temple courtyard had turned into a market, with sellers and money changers working the crowds who came to pray.
days.means: Jesus gets angry about what people do to the place where God meets them. You are a temple too. Whatever has set up shop in there and crowded out prayer, he wants to clear it out.
days.today: Clear one thing out of your day that crowds out God, even for ten minutes.
days.say: Jesus, walk into my heart and clear out what doesn't belong there. Make me a house of prayer. Amen.

days.day: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary on Saturday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.name: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
days.week: Saturday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And there came to him some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is any resurrection, and they asked him,
Saying: Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any man’s brother die, having a wife, and he leave no children, that his brother should take her to wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.
And the next took her to wife, and he also died childless.
And the third took her. And in like manner all the seven, and they left no children, and died.
Last of all the woman died also.
In the resurrection therefore, whose wife of them shall she be? For all the seven had her to wife.
And Jesus said to them: The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:
But they that shall be accounted worthy of that world, and of the resurrection from the dead, shall neither be married, nor take wives.
Neither can they die any more: for they are equal to the angels, and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.
Now that the dead rise again, Moses also shewed, at the bush, when he called the Lord, The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob;
For he is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for all live to him.
And some of the scribes answering, said to him: Master, thou hast said well.
And after that they durst not ask him any more questions.

saint.name: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saint.about: An old tradition, not from the Bible but from an early Christian writing, says Mary's parents, Joachim and Anne, brought her to the Temple in Jerusalem as a little girl to give her to God. The Church keeps this day to honor how Mary belonged to God from the very start.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: For he is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for all live to him.

days.title: GOD OF THE LIVING
days.t: Some people tried to trap Jesus with a trick question about heaven. He told them the dead are alive to God.
days.where: The Sadducees, a group of priests who didn't believe in the resurrection, make up a story about a woman married seven times to make the whole idea sound silly. Jesus answers them straight from Moses.
days.means: Heaven isn't just this life on repeat. It's something bigger than we can picture. And the people we've lost aren't gone to God. Everybody you pray for is alive to him.
days.today: Say a prayer for someone you've lost, by name.
days.say: God of the living, hold the people I miss close to you. Let me see them again someday. Amen.

days.name: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And when the Son of man shall come in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then shall he sit upon the seat of his majesty.
And all nations shall be gathered together before him, and he shall separate them one from another, as the shepherd separateth the sheep from the goats:
And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on his left.
Then shall the king say to them that shall be on his right hand: Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry, and you gave me to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink; I was a stranger, and you took me in:
Naked, and you covered me: sick, and you visited me: I was in prison, and you came to me.
Then shall the just answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see thee hungry, and fed thee; thirsty, and gave thee drink?
And when did we see thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and covered thee?
Or when did we see thee sick or in prison, and came to thee?
And the king answering, shall say to them: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.
Then he shall say to them also that shall be on his left hand: Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire which was prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry, and you gave me not to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave me not to drink.
I was a stranger, and you took me not in: naked, and you covered me not: sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.
Then they also shall answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see thee hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to thee?
Then he shall answer them, saying: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it not to one of these least, neither did you do it to me.
And these shall go into everlasting punishment: but the just, into life everlasting.

saint.name: Christ the King
saint.about: Pope Pius XI started this feast in 1925, when dictators and big governments were trying to take the place of God. It says no leader, party or paycheck gets the last word: Jesus does. It's the last Sunday of the Church year.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.

days.title: THE KING IN DISGUISE
days.t: The King of everything shows up as the hungry guy, the stranger, the one in jail. How you treat them is how you treat him.
days.where: Jesus tells this right before his Passion: at the end, the Son of Man sits as king and sorts people like a shepherd sorts sheep from goats. The surprise is that nobody on either side knew it was him.
days.means: Today closes out the Church's year, and next Sunday Advent starts. Christ is King, but his throne room is the street. Feeding someone, visiting someone, showing up for someone is serving the King himself.
days.today: Do one thing for somebody who can't pay you back: food, a ride, a visit, a call.
days.say: Jesus, my King, help me see you in the people everybody else walks past. Rule my heart. Amen.

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And looking on, he saw the rich men cast their gifts into the treasury.
And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in two brass mites.
And he said: Verily I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
For all these have of their abundance cast into the offerings of God: but she of her want, hath cast in all the living that she had.

saint.name: Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro
saint.about: A Mexican Jesuit priest who said Mass and gave the sacraments in secret, in disguises, when the government of Mexico was persecuting the Church. He was executed by firing squad in Mexico City, his arms stretched out like a cross, saying 'Viva Cristo Rey,' long live Christ the King.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Verily I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all

days.title: TWO LITTLE COINS
days.t: Rich people drop big gifts in the Temple box. A poor widow drops two tiny coins, and Jesus says she gave the most.
days.where: Jesus is in the Temple in Jerusalem during his last days, watching people bring their offerings. The widow's two coins were the smallest money there was, and it was everything she had to live on.
days.means: God doesn't count it like we do. He looks at the heart behind the gift. Small and all-in beats big and leftover, whether it's money, time or love.
days.today: Give somebody your full attention today, phone down, even if it's only five minutes.
days.say: Lord, I don't have much, but what I have is yours. Take it all. Amen.

days.day: Saints Andrew Dũng-Lạc and his Companions, Martyrs on Tuesday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Saints Andrew Dũng-Lạc and Companions
days.week: Tuesday of week 34 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And some saying of the temple, that it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said:
These things which you see, the days will come in which there shall not be left a stone upon a stone that shall not be thrown down.
And they asked him, saying: Master, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when they shall begin to come to pass?
Who said: Take heed you be not seduced; for many will come in my name, saying, I am he; and the time is at hand: go ye not therefore after them.
And when you shall hear of wars and seditions, be not terrified: these things must first come to pass; but the end is not yet presently.
Then he said to them: Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
And there shall be great earthquakes in divers places, and pestilences, and famines, and terrors from heaven; and there shall be great signs.

saint.name: Saints Andrew Dũng-Lạc and Companions
saint.about: 117 martyrs of Vietnam: priests, catechists, mothers, fathers and soldiers killed for the faith over more than a hundred years. Andrew Dũng-Lạc was a Vietnamese priest who was beheaded in 1839. Saint John Paul II made them saints in 1988.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: And when you shall hear of wars and seditions, be not terrified

days.title: DON'T PANIC
days.t: Jesus says scary days will come, wars and earthquakes and all of it. And he says don't be terrified.
days.where: People are admiring how beautiful the Temple is, and Jesus tells them it will be torn down. He's talking near the end of his life about hard times coming for the world and for his followers.
days.means: Bad news doesn't mean God lost control. Jesus told us ahead of time so we wouldn't freak out or follow whoever yells the loudest. Fear doesn't get to drive.
days.today: Take a break from the news or the feed today and pray for one place that's hurting.
days.say: Jesus, when the world feels like it's falling apart, keep me calm and close to you. Amen.
